main_text.p: paretis femen calore,ficcitateq; plurimum excellat,mas procreabitur: contra si frigus humorque uincat & exuperet, foemina.

Quod utiq; confirmat philosophus libro, quarto, de Generatione animaliu,ubi mare m in quacunque animalis specie foemina esse calidiorem profert. Idem quoq; Galenus libro secundo, de feminę sentire uidetur,ubi foeminam esse humidiorem & frigidiorem,mascu lum uero calidiorem & ficciorem perspicue demonstrat. Septimo ite libro,de Visu partium omnes foeminas masculis esse frigidiores concludit. Quod autem sint huiusmodi foeminae,patet ratione. Nam ipsas masculis debiliores esse omnibus satis constat. At uirium robur calorina tiuo & spiritibus tribui par est. Propterea omnes foeminae maribus sunt frigidiores.

Adhaec omnes foeminae pilos producunt, & planiores, & tenuiores. Atqui tales pilos fieri a debiliori calore latis est manifestum. Nam quo intensior calor est, eo magis pilos & exiccat,& incraffat atq; crispos reddit.
Deinde foeminae uafa habent minora, quam masculi.Sed amplitudinem uasorum a calore fieri neminem medicu philosophum latet.

page.notes: Transcription is from a small, low-resolution scan; the last word of the final line is cut off by the fold at the right edge, so "edunt," is read as printed. Word-level doubtful readings: the line "Quod utiq; confirmat" is partly obscured, "ficciorem" and "calore latis" are uncertain, and several long-s and u/v readings in the sixth and seventh lines ("uirium", "uasorum", "intensior") rest on a faint image. The marks "»" in the left margin are typographic line-openers, not notes, and are omitted. Lines were joined into paragraphs where they run full width without an indent; the sentence-level text of the printed paragraph break before "Deinde" and "Demum" is taken from the indentation visible on the scan.
